cards.stem: What term describes the tendency to resist changes in a state of motion?
options: inertia
momentum
acceleration
thrust
cards.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.
cards.hint: Focus on the word for resistance to change in motion.

cards.stem: What does Newton's first law state about an object with no net force acting?
options: An object at rest remains at rest
depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied
exerts an equal and opposite force on the first
is defined to be the mass m of an object times its velocity V
cards.quote: An object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line
cards.hint: Recall what happens without a net force.

cards.stem: What determines the acceleration of an object according to Newton's second law?
options: depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied
remains at rest unless acted on by an unbalanced force
exerts an equal and opposite on the first
resist changes in a state of motion is inertia
cards.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

cards.stem: What happens when one object exerts a force on another object?
options: the second object exerts an equal and opposite on the first
An object at rest remains at rest
The acceleration depends on the mass of the object
This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia
cards.quote: Whenever one object exerts a force on another object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite on the first.
